samples.prompt: Why might people support the proposal that communities should make everyday walking more convenient? Is this a positive or negative development?

samples.summaryVi: Đi bộ dễ thành thói quen khi đường tới nơi cần đến thuận tiện và không bị cản trở.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: There are understandable reasons why people may support the proposal that communities should make everyday walking more convenient. I consider this a mainly positive development when it is organised with practical needs in mind. Its value comes from the help it can offer in daily life, rather than from the idea simply sounding modern or attractive.

paragraphs.label: Câu hỏi 1 — vì sao?
paragraphs.text: One important point in favour of the proposal is that people can include gentle movement in ordinary routines. This is possible because a useful route to a shop or bus stop can make walking part of a journey rather than an extra task. For example, a resident can walk to a nearby market instead of taking a motorbike for a very short trip. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.

paragraphs.label: Câu hỏi 2 — đánh giá
paragraphs.text: I see the development as positive because it gives people a useful option, provided that the main obstacles are recognised. One concern is that an ambitious hobby plan can become another source of pressure. This is connected with the fact that people may compare their starting point with experienced hobbyists. Ignoring that concern would weaken the case for the proposal, so support should include an effort to improve how it works.

paragraphs.label: Ví dụ về điều kiện
paragraphs.text: A practical response would be to begin with small goals and choose an affordable way to practise. For example, a beginner could borrow equipment and practise one simple skill for a short time each week. This approach is useful because it deals with a specific obstacle instead of simply repeating a general message. It could first be tried on a small scale, with feedback from the people involved, and then adjusted if some needs have been overlooked.

paragraphs.text: In conclusion, people have good reason to support this approach because a hobby can provide a break from work and routine responsibilities. I regard it as mainly positive, but the result depends on practical planning. A flexible approach that listens to the people involved is more likely to deliver the intended value.
